- When sentiment is consistently low (avg < 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10% below peak or use 2-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive days < 0.4), model underestimates downward trend; add 2–4% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply 5–8% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is high (avg > 0.7) and price is trending up, model often fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast slope by 15–20% after 10-day horizon.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.25 range over 3 days), model exhibits erratic behavior; use sentiment-weighted average of last 5 days to anchor forecast.
